text: Once again Jesus began teaching by the lake, and such a large crowd gathered around him that he got into a boat on the water and sat there, while the whole crowd stood on the shore.
He taught them at length using parables, and among what he taught them was this:
Listen! A farmer went out to sow seed.
As he scattered it, some seed fell along the path, and birds came and ate it up.
Other seed fell on rocky ground where there wasn't much soil, and it sprang up quickly because the soil had no depth.
But when the sun rose, it was scorched, and because it had no root it withered away.
Other seed fell among thorn bushes, and the thorns grew up and choked it, so it produced no grain.
Still other seed fell on good soil, came up, grew, and produced a crop — thirty, sixty, even a hundred times what was sown.
Then he said, Let the one who has ears to hear, listen.
When he was alone, those around him along with the twelve asked him about the parables.
He told them, To you the secret of God's kingdom has been given, but to those outside, everything comes in parables,
so that they may look and look but not truly see, and listen and listen but not understand — otherwise they might turn back and be forgiven.
Then he asked them, Don't you understand this parable? Then how will you understand any of the parables?
The farmer sows the word.
Some are like seed on the path: as soon as they hear the word, Satan comes at once and snatches away what was sown in them.
Others are like seed on rocky ground: they hear the word and receive it right away with joy,
but they have no root, so they don't last — when trouble or persecution comes because of the word, they quickly fall away.
Still others are like seed sown among thorns: they hear the word,
but the worries of life, the lure of wealth, and cravings for other things creep in and choke the word, so it produces nothing.
And others are like seed sown on good soil: they hear the word, accept it, and produce a crop — thirty, sixty, even a hundred times what was sown.
He also asked them, Does anyone bring in a lamp to put it under a basket or under the bed? No — it's put on a stand.
For nothing is hidden except to be brought into the open, and nothing is concealed except to come out into the light.
If anyone has ears to hear, let them listen.
He told them, Pay attention to what you hear: the measure you use will be measured back to you, and even more besides.
Whoever has will be given more, and whoever has nothing, even what little they have will be taken from them.
He said, God's kingdom is like this: a man scatters seed on the ground.
He sleeps and gets up, night after night and day after day, and the seed sprouts and grows without his understanding how it happens.
The earth produces a crop all by itself — first the stalk, then the head, then the full grain in the head.
As soon as the grain is ripe, he puts the sickle to it, because harvest has come.
He also asked, What can we compare God's kingdom to, or what story can capture it?
It's like a mustard seed, which, when planted, is smaller than every other seed on earth.
But once it's planted, it grows up and becomes bigger than every garden plant, with branches large enough that birds can nest in its shade.
With many such parables he spoke the word to them, as much as they were able to understand,
and he did not speak to them without using a parable — though privately, he explained everything to his own disciples.
That evening, he told them, Let's cross over to the other side.
Leaving the crowd behind, they took him along in the boat, just as he was, and other boats went with him.
A fierce windstorm arose, and waves were breaking into the boat so that it was already filling with water.
Jesus, meanwhile, was in the back of the boat, sleeping on a cushion. They woke him and said, Teacher, don't you care that we're about to drown?
He got up, rebuked the wind, and told the sea, Quiet! Be still! The wind died down, and it became completely calm.
He asked them, Why are you so afraid? Do you still have no faith?
Overcome with fear, they said to one another, Who is this, then, that even the wind and the sea obey him?
